questions.scenario: Two of your classmates are fighting fiercely. What is your role?

options.text: Step in powerfully and order them to stop.
Listen to both sides and decide who is actually right.
Suggest a new class rule so this doesn't happen again.
Take them to the teacher and help sort it out calmly.
Act as a neutral mediator and negotiate a peaceful compromise between them.
None of these.

questions.scenario: While playing a board game (like Monopoly or Ludo) with friends, you are the one who...

options.text: Makes sure everyone plays by the rules strictly.
Argues with logic if someone tries to cheat.
Reads the rulebook deeply to find the smartest strategy.
Manages the game's bank and distributes the money.
Forms smart alliances, negotiates clever trades, and uses diplomacy to win.
None of these.

questions.scenario: A grand school trip is being planned. What responsibility do you take?

options.text: The Captain: Leading the group and giving directions.
The Defender: Making sure nobody is bullied or left out.
The Planner: Researching the route, budget, and timetable.
The Manager: Counting heads, distributing tickets and snacks.
The Ambassador: Talking to the locals, guides, and representing our school well.
None of these.

questions.scenario: When you watch a superhero or action movie, which scene gives you goosebumps?

options.text: The hero bravely stopping the chaos in the city.
The intense courtroom scene where the villain is exposed.
The hero sitting in a secret base, planning a master strategy.
The hero helping normal, common people on the streets.
The tense negotiation scene where a massive global war is stopped through smart dialogue.
None of these.

questions.scenario: Your friend is punished by a teacher for a mistake they didn't do. You will...

options.text: Directly approach the Principal to take action.
Collect solid proof and debate with the teacher.
Write a strong application to change the punishment system.
Comfort the friend and find a practical way out of the mess.
Have a highly polite and diplomatic conversation with the teacher to negotiate a pardon.
None of these.

questions.scenario: If you had a superpower, what would it be?

options.text: Authority: When I speak, people automatically listen.
Logic: Nobody can ever defeat me in an argument.
Vision: I can predict the long-term future perfectly.
Multitasking: I can handle 10 different people at once.
Persuasion: I can smoothly calm any conflict and make rival groups agree with each other.
None of these.

questions.scenario: There is a massive crowd at a concert and the exit gate is jammed. What do you do?

options.text: Stand on a chair and loudly command the crowd to step back.
Find out whose fault this is and hold them accountable later.
Think about a better, safer gate design for the next concert.
Form a human chain to pull people out safely one by one.
Use a loudspeaker to calmly communicate and coordinate with different groups to ease the panic.
None of these.

questions.scenario: What kind of books or documentaries do you find interesting?

options.text: Biographies of powerful leaders, kings, and generals.
Mystery, crime-solving, and detective stories.
History, geography, and how the world economy works.
Real-life stories of everyday local heroes.
Stories about international relations, global treaties, and how different countries interact.
None of these.

questions.scenario: Every job has a boring part. Which of these can you tolerate easily?

options.text: Standing for hours to ensure an event goes perfectly.
Reading 100 pages of boring rules to find one small mistake.
Writing a 20-page detailed report on a city problem.
Listening to 50 complaining people one by one.
Sitting through hours of polite, formal meetings and smiling even with people I disagree with.
None of these.

questions.scenario: In your friend group, what title fits you the best?

options.text: The Boss (Decision Maker).
The Judge (Truth Finder).
The Brain (The Planner).
The Fixer (The Ground Worker).
The Diplomat (The Peacemaker and Negotiator).
None of these.
